old: Its ancient root simply meant 'order' — the same order that gives the universe its name.
It traces to a Greek word meaning to arrange, adorn, or equip.
It's a linguistic sibling of 'cosmos,' both born from the idea of putting things in order.
clues: This adjective describes a certain kind of change or improvement. It grew from an ancient Greek word meaning simply 'order,' the same root behind a word for the whole universe.
It describes changes that improve only how something looks, not how it works, and often hints they are merely skin-deep. Its Greek ancestor named the art of dress and ornament.
Plastic surgeons offer this kind of surgery, and as a plural noun it names lipstick, mascara and foundation. It shares its deepest root with 'cosmos.'
